Hi, I am new to R language, I am trying to run a SEM for model with both continous and count data. I know that Lavaan can not directly deal with count data and my model may need to be dealt with Generalized SEM model in STATA. But can i run a factor analysis for the count data to extract the latent variable, and then place the latent variable in regular SEM with the rest of variable being continous variables? if I can do that, what estimator can I use? is there any paper explictly using this method as well? 

Thanks very much for reading this, I really appreiciate you guys answer!!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: count data and continous data in SEM
parts: can i run a factor analysis for the count data

Using what?  Mplus?  If you have access to that, I'm not sure why you wouldn't fit your full SEM using Mplus.

to extract the latent variable, and then place the latent variable in regular SEM with the rest of variable being continuous variables?

If you want to trust your SEs, you need to account for the uncertainty about factor-score estimates.  You can obtain "plausible values" using Mplus:

https://statmodel.com/download/Plausible.pdf
if I can do that, what estimator can I use?

You can use ML(M/R), but you need to use multiple-imputation methods to pool results across plausible values.  You can use semTools for that (see ?runMI).
